design_status: Fixed before v29 calculation; post-hoc sensitivity after v27.
question: Does BUB1B specificity survive symmetric out-of-fit comparisons and CRISPR QC restriction?
source: v25 public prepared matrices; same experimental wells as prior cycles
split: SHA256(str(seed)+":"+gene) integer mod 5; same gene assigned same fold in both modalities.
aggregation: Arithmetic mean by target/cell in each modality, as v25; CRISPR 96h; no invented RNAi QC.
projection: Rank normalize 978 features. Exclude all query genes and current held-out fold from training in both modalities. Fit pooled mean direction and first 10 residual PCs. Evaluate ONLY held-out references plus query genes. Never combine correlation scales across folds.
comparisons: Both cross-modal retrieval directions; same-cell identity-matched everolimus and MTOR profiles. Preserve separate drug/query QC and dose/time. No joint-rescue claim.
outputs: all query correlation/rank/count records across 400 fitted folds and four representations
full held-out shared-gene panel, separately retained locally
held-out same-target top1/top10 retrieval counts as quality context
missing query cells explicit, never zero-filled
unadjusted all-profile full-panel values must match v27
controls: train/evaluation target sets disjoint in each modality
all ordinary reference genes evaluated once per seed
CPU FP64 vs CUDA FP32 subset <=2e-5
one known reference query MTOR and all eight other query targets retained
limitations: Same source experiments; no new guide or biological replication.
Repeated partitions and PC removal are sensitivity checks, not confidence intervals or causal adjustment.
Removal can discard true biology. Held-out ranks have smaller denominators than original all-gene ranks.
QC-only applies to CRISPR profiles; RNAi potency/seed controls remain unresolved.
No operational threshold selected to promote HT29 or drug response.
